description: Exact canonical URLs for the settlement-systems (VIBER/BKR/KELER) release, the Pénzforgalom 2030 PDF, and the archive index were inferred from parent pages rather than fetched individually.
The workbook layer (sheet names, indicator granularity, history depth, revision policy) of the quarterly payments release was not inspected.
Denomination-level banknote/coin volume time series (as opposed to the aggregate value of currency in circulation) were not located as a downloadable dataset.
MNB supervisory statistics (felügyeleti statisztikák) and payment-oversight/enforcement publications were not explored, though they may carry institution-level payment and card acquiring detail.
It is unknown which fields the Intézménykereső exposes per entity (licence number, activity codes, licence date, status, address, ownership) and whether historic/withdrawn licences remain queryable.

Registers likely relevant to the payments actor map were not explored in this cell: virtual-asset/crypto service provider registration under MiCA, the MNB's cash-processing (készpénzfeldolgozó) authorisations, and the payment/securities settlement system oversight lists (GIRO, KELER, VIBER operators).
For several HU-language sources (Fizetési rendszer jelentés, FinTech report, Aranykönyv, decisions search) the exact English-edition URLs were not captured, only their existence inferred.
An MNB archive tree (www.mnb.hu/archivum/...) holds legacy PSZAF-era supervisory statistics including older Aranykönyv editions, but its structure and coverage span were not mapped.

Retail/commerce trade press (e.g. Trade magazin, Piac és Profit, Növekedés.hu) was not searched; these carry merchant-side acceptance, cash-handling and checkout-technology data that banking media omit.

English-language Hungary-focused business media (Budapest Business Journal / bbj.hu, Hungary Today, Daily News Hungary, Telex English) was not covered in this slice; searches skewed hu-language by design.

Journalist-level and newsletter-level sources (named banking correspondents, Portfolio/FinTechZone conference agendas and speaker lists, LinkedIn/Substack-style analyst newsletters) were not mapped, though these are where leaks and pre-publication figures first appear.
No assessment was made of historical archive depth or paywall boundaries for Portfolio.hu, bonline.hu/vg.hu and hvg360 — critical for building any back-series of media-reported figures.
Only Bankmonitor, Bank360, Biztosdöntés and Money.hu were captured; other HU comparison/aggregator brands (e.g. Bankráció, Bankszamla-focused aggregators) were not enumerated.

Mid-tier and boutique advisory/research actors were not systematically enumerated: Roland Berger Hungary, Bain/BCG Budapest, Századvég, Policy Agenda, Ipsos Hungary, Kantar Hoffmann, Median, Publicus — several of which run omnibus surveys that could carry payment questions.

Almost nothing surfaced from consultancies or academia specifically on ATM and POS terminal estate economics (acceptance-network sizing, ATM interchange, merchant acquiring cost studies) — the searches skewed to consumer payment behaviour.
No page in this cell was fetched and confirmed; all candidates rest on search-result evidence. Gating (registration walls on KPMG/Deloitte report downloads) is inferred, not observed.

English-language Hungary-focused academic output (e.g. Corvinus and CEU working papers in EN, international journals with HU payment datasets) was only lightly probed; EN coverage of this cell is thinner than HU.
No aggregator/archive was identified that systematically indexes Hungarian consultancy reports (as opposed to news mentions) — discovery currently depends on trade media noticing a release.
Magyar Posta's role as a cash-access channel (post office cash withdrawal, Posta-operated ATMs, rural cash provision) was not investigated in this pass.
Bank-side disclosures on ATM estate size and cash-handling cost (OTP, MBH, Erste, K&H, Raiffeisen, UniCredit annual reports and investor presentations) not yet mapped.
Cash-recycling hardware and retail cashback/cash-at-POS as alternative cash-cycle channels are unmapped (Glory, CIMA, retail chain disclosures).
European-level comparators (ECB SDW/Payments Statistics, ECB banknote data) that place HU ATM density and cash-per-ATM in context were not enumerated in this cell.
Company-level financials require e-beszámoló form interaction or paid registry access; no bulk-extraction route established.
No confirmed monthly/quarterly official series for transaction-levy receipts.
MNB supervisory decision/sanction register (határozatok, bírságok) for payment and IFR breaches was not indexed as a distinct source.
GVH (Gazdasági Versenyhivatal) case and decision database not covered for card-fee and payment-market cases.
Rules obliging public bodies/tax offices to accept card payment (POS at Kormányablak/NAV) and the surcharging ban were not separately searched.
English-language coverage of Hungarian legislative/fiscal channels is thin: most primary material exists only in Hungarian; only EUR-Lex and MNB English publications were captured.
Professional-network channel (LinkedIn company pages and personal posts of MNB/GIRO/bank payment executives) is unaddressed.
Vendor/ISO side of the HU POS and ATM market (terminal suppliers, ATM maintainers, payment software integrators, cash-in-transit firms) was not systematically enumerated; only Euronet was captured.
Hungarian domestic procurement register (EKR / Közbeszerzési Értesítő) was inferred as relevant but not directly located or profiled in this pass; only the EU-level TED notice was seen.

Awards coverage is limited to the Mastercard Év Bankja programme; other HU/CEE award schemes that surface payment projects (e.g. IT/innovation and e-commerce awards, CEE-level fintech awards) were not enumerated.
Conference and award sources are annual/episodic; archived past editions (agendas, slide decks) were not harvested, so no historical baseline exists for detecting what is genuinely new.
The individual file-level contents of the six MNB 'archív tartalmak' sub-pages (exact XLS files, year coverage, column definitions) were not enumerated in this pass.
No CDX enumeration of Wayback captures for mnb.hu, statisztika.mnb.hu, giro.hu, keler.hu or bankszovetseg.hu was performed.
Commercial-bank and association archives (Magyar Bankszövetség yearbooks, KELER, Takarékbank/OTP investor archives) and MABISZ-style sector reports were not searched in this cell.
BIS CPMI Red Book statistics and IMF Financial Access Survey historical HU card/ATM/POS series were not searched, though both retain long back-runs.
Academic/research repositories (Zenodo, OSF, REAL/MTA repository, university dataverses) that may host replication datasets of Hungarian payment studies were not covered.
Whether NAV would release aggregated, anonymised cash-register payment-mode statistics under a public-interest data request (közérdekű adatigénylés) is unknown and untested.

The legal instruments defining online cash register and e-receipt data content (the cash-register decrees and the e-receipt implementing rules) were not retrieved in this pass, so the exact reported fields — including whether payment mode is a mandatory data element — remain unconfirmed.

Cash-register distributor/servicer registers and the population of registered online cash registers by sector (a direct proxy for the merchant acceptance base alongside POS terminals) were not enumerated in this pass.

Ministry-level sources (Nemzetgazdasági Minisztérium / Pénzügyminisztérium) and the Magyar Államkincstár were only lightly touched; their fiscal and disbursement statistics (e.g. state payments, treasury cash flows) could add non-central-bank payment signal.

Several URLs (KSH publication paths, the Statisztikai Szemle hub, pei.nav.gov.hu) were derived from search result listings rather than direct fetch, so their current liveness and exact paths are unconfirmed.
Current (2023–2026) GIRO-published BKR/GIROInstant monthly volume series has not been located; only MNB's quarterly aggregates are confirmed as an alternative.

Peripheral HU/regional infrastructure actors were not searched in this pass: the postal payment channel (Magyar Posta / Posta Elszámoló Központ), CLS settlement exposure for HUF, TARGET2/T2 and TIPS participation by Hungarian institutions, and the ACH/instant vendor layer behind GIROInstant.

No PFMI / CPMI-IOSCO disclosure framework document or system self-assessment for BKR, GIROInstant or KELER CSD/CCP was located, although systemically important FMIs are normally expected to publish one.
The English-language mirrors (giro.hu/en, keler.hu English site, MNB English statistics portal) were noted but not systematically mapped; equivalence between HU and EN document sets is unconfirmed.
All URLs in this slice are search- or fetch-derived candidates; several (notably hashed giro.hu /storage/ asset paths and accented keler.hu paths) are fragile and were not liveness-checked here.

Savings-cooperative and integration bodies (Szövetkezeti Hitelintézetek Integrációs Szervezete, OTSZ/Takarékszövetkezetek heritage bodies) were seen only as EFISZ founding members and Bankszövetség member entries; their own association sites were not searched.

Peak employer/business confederations (MGYOSZ/BusinessHungary, VOSZ, Magyar Kereskedelmi Szövetségek in hospitality such as MVI, and the payment-adjacent Magyar Vendéglátók Ipartestülete) were not covered; they are cash-intensive-sector voices on cash-acceptance mandates.
Member directories for HFA and EFISZ, and the Bankszövetség working-group/committee structure (which would reveal the payments-specific subgroups), remain unenumerated.

No archival strategy established for association content: association sites rewrite news indexes and PDFs disappear, and no Wayback/OSZK (EPA) mirroring was checked beyond noting REAL-J holds Gazdaság és Pénzügy issues.
No English-language association output was located other than EFISZ's /en/ section; whether Bankszövetség, OKSZ or MKIK maintain English pages was not confirmed.

Visa's and Mastercard's Hungary-relevant investor/statistical disclosures (global operating performance data, Europe region volumes) were not scouted in this pass — only the HU consumer-facing press rooms were covered.

Domestic-scheme and infrastructure actors adjacent to the cell were not covered: GIRO Zrt. / GIROInstant (instant payment infrastructure) and the Hungarian ATM-siting subsidy programme operator, plus Revolut/Wise as non-bank card issuers/acquirers gaining HU share.
Most HU terminal/ATM operator numbers found are point-in-time marketing claims (2016, 2020, 2022) with no continuous series; no operator publishes a regular HU statistical release.
Market-share figures for HU acquirers and PSPs exist only as unsourced trade/agency estimates; no authoritative public acquirer-level market-share source was identified.
Nexi's Hungarian-language communications were not located; the confirmed material for the Nexi HU entity was English (nexicentraleurope.com) or register listings.

Bank-owned payment subsidiaries and acquiring arms were not separately scouted in this run — notably OTP Mobil (SimplePay), OTP's merchant-acquiring unit, and any MBH/Erste payment service entities. These file their own statutory accounts and often disclose transaction volumes their parent bank does not.

Cash usage from the bank side (ATM cash withdrawal volumes, branch cash handling, cash-recycler deployment) was not located in any bank-published source found here; banks disclose network size but not cash throughput.

ESEF/iXBRL filings (observed for OTP and UniCredit Jelzálogbank) were noted but not evaluated for whether they carry any of the operational KPIs of interest; they are structured but likely financial-statement-only.
Only three of the eight cell banks publish quarterly; the rest are annual-only, so any bank-side card/digital series will be annual with a 3-5 month publication lag.
Several HU banks publish HU and EN versions of the same report with differing detail; it was not established which language version is authoritative or more complete per bank.

State-owned and state-influenced banks (e.g. MBH Bank group entities, Magyar Fejlesztési Bank, Takarék entities, Magyar Posta's financial arms, Diákhitel Központ) were not individually checked for buyer-profile procurement pages or as 'ajánlatkérő' in the procurement registry.

No CPV-code-driven sweep was executed; the pass relied on keyword search. CPV families for cash dispensers, payment/banking terminals, smart cards, card production, cash-in-transit security services and banking software were not enumerated against HU notices.

Municipal and utility contracting entities (parking companies, water/energy utilities, hospitals, universities) that buy card-accepting terminals, parking payment machines and cash-desk systems were not sampled.

Remedies and dispute channels (Közbeszerzési Döntőbizottság decisions, Állami Számvevőszék audits of procurement, court/appeal records) were identified only via the registries hub, not individually located as sources.

Hungarian-language coverage was strong for ATM/cash terms, but no local-language terms were exercised for card personalisation and card issuing ('kártyaszemélyesítés', 'kártyagyártás', 'chipkártya', 'kártyakibocsátás') or for payment IT ('kártyaelfogadói rendszer', 'tranzakciós switch', 'ATM monitoring rendszer').

Contract-modification notices ('szerződésmódosításról szóló tájékoztató') and performance/completion notices were not treated as a distinct collection stream, although they are where actual delivered quantities and extended fleet counts appear.
POS terminal hardware vendors (Ingenico/Worldline, Verifone, PAX, Castles) and their HU distributors/bank customers were not covered in this pass.

Central infrastructure operators that sit between banks and vendors (GIRO Zrt., BISZ Zrt., Bankkártya/scheme processors) were not profiled, though their supplier announcements name participating private banks.
Vendor case-study libraries were reached via search engines only; no direct in-site case-study search (site: queries, sitemap crawl) was performed for the major vendors.
Few vendor sources found so far disclose HU-specific unit counts; the Diebold/UniCredit ~180 ATM figure and the MNB-mandated 1,039-unit allocation are the main quantified anchors.

Hungarian-language searching worked well for cash logistics, ATM mandates and domestic integrators, but produced almost nothing for card-personalisation contract news and nothing for international vendor case studies (which exist in English only).
The exact ECB SDMX dataflow keys carrying Hungarian ATM/POS terminal and card-transaction series (PSD vs legacy PTN/PTT) were not enumerated in this pass.
OECD and the European Commission's DESI / Digital Decade reporting were not investigated, though both re-publish Hungarian digital-payment and e-commerce indicators.
European Payments Council (SEPA scheme adherence/statistics) and the ECB's TARGET/TIPS and instant-payments reporting, which cover Hungarian PSP participation, were not covered.
Findex microdata (microdata.worldbank.org catalog 7860) likely requires account creation and terms acceptance, which an automated collector must not perform.
No URL in this slice was fetched for liveness; all are recorded from search-result evidence and portal structure.
